property_summary: For any oracle address stored in the product, C.currentVersion() always returns the oracle version after applying the product's payoff transformation (i.e. transformed price), whereas the mutant returns the raw untransformed oracle version — so there exists an oracle version whose price differs from its transformed price and thus the two return values differ.

For every deployed product C with any oracle address and payoff definition, C.currentVersion() always returns an OracleVersion whose price equals payoffDefinition.transform(oracle.currentVersion().price); the mutant that returns oracle().currentVersion() (untransformed) will differ for any oracle version where transform changes the price (fuzzer will find such a price).

For any oracle version price, C.currentVersion() always returns the oracle version with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition (i.e. transformed price equals payoffDefinition.transform(raw price)); the mutant that returns oracle().currentVersion() returns the untransformed price and thus will differ for any input where the transform changes the price.

For any oracle version returned by the underlying oracle, the product's currentVersion() returns that same version but with its price replaced by payoffDefinition.transform(rawPrice); the mutant that returns oracle().currentVersion() returns the raw (untransformed) price and thus can differ whenever transform(rawPrice) != rawPrice.

For any oracle address and payoff definition, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle's currentVersion() with its price run through payoffDefinition.transform (i.e., transformed.price == payoffDefinition.transform(raw.price)); the mutant returns the raw oracle version (untransformed), so there exist oracle versions whose price changes under transform and thus the two return values differ.

For every oracleVersion input, C.atVersion(oracleVersion) returns an OracleVersion whose price equals the payoffDefinition-transformed oracle.price (i.e., C applies payoffDefinition.transform); the mutant returns the raw oracle price, so there exists an oracleVersion where the transformed price differs and the mutant breaks this rule.

For every oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns an OracleVersion whose price equals payoffDefinition.transform(rawOracle.price) (i.e., C always applies the payoff transform); the mutant returns the raw oracle price and thus will produce a different price for some oracleVersion.

For any oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns successfully and its returned price equals the payoffDefinition-transformed price provided by the oracle provider; the mutant returns the raw oracle price (not transformed) for some oracleVersion, so there exists an id where the returned price differs causing the property to fail.

For every oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns an OracleVersion whose price equals the payoffDefinition.transform(...) of the underlying oracle provider's price; the mutant returns the raw oracle price (no transform) and thus will differ for some oracleVersion/price.

For every oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns successfully and the returned OracleVersion.price equals the payoffDefinition-transformed price from the underlying oracle provider; the mutant returns the raw oracle provider price (no transform) for some oracleVersion, so the property is violated for those inputs.

For any product instance, maintenance(account) must return the stored maintenance parameter (controller-visible product maintenance) — the mutant that returns a constant ZERO will produce a different return for some maintenance values.

For any stored maintenance value set during initialize, calling maintenance(account) returns that stored maintenance; the mutant always returns ZERO so for some initialized maintenance this will differ.

For any fuzzed nonzero maintenance value supplied to initialize, the correct contract returns that stored maintenance via maintenance(account) for any account, whereas the mutant that always returns ZERO will differ whenever the initialized maintenance is nonzero.

For any nonzero maintenance parameter used to initialize the product, the reference contract's maintenance(account) returns that stored maintenance for every account, while the mutant that always returns UFixed18Lib.ZERO will differ whenever the initialized maintenance is nonzero.

For any initialized nonzero maintenance parameter, calling maintenance(account) on the correct contract returns that stored maintenance (same for any account); the mutant that always returns UFixed18Lib.ZERO will differ whenever the initialized maintenance is nonzero.

For any contract state, C.maintenance() returns the product's stored maintenance parameter; the mutant returns makerLimit() instead, so there exist inputs where maintenance() != makerLimit() causing the mutant to differ.

For every product state, maintenance() must equal the stored maintenance parameter; the mutant returns makerLimit() instead, so there exist states where maintenance() != makerLimit() and the mutant will return a different value.

For any product state, maintenance() returns the stored maintenance parameter; the mutant returns makerLimit() instead, so there exist states where maintenance() != makerLimit() and the mutant will return a different value.

For any product state, calling maintenance(account) returns the stored maintenance parameter; the mutant returns makerLimit() instead, so whenever maintenance() != makerLimit() the mutant will return a different value and the property is violated.

For any product state, the public getter maintenance() returns the stored maintenance parameter; the mutant returns makerLimit() instead, so there exist inputs (makerLimit != maintenance) where maintenance() != makerLimit() and the mutant will return a different value.

For any product instance, maintenance() must return the stored maintenance parameter (the value set at initialization or via updates); the mutant returns fundingFee() instead, so for some inputs (distinct maintenance and fundingFee values) maintenance() will differ.

For every ProductInfo used to initialize C, maintenance() must return the maintenance value supplied at initialize; the mutant returns fundingFee() instead, so when maintenance != fundingFee the mutant will return a different value.

For every initialization ProductInfo, C.maintenance() returns the maintenance value passed at initialize; the mutant returns fundingFee() instead, so when the fuzzed maintenance and fundingFee differ the mutant will return a different value.

For any pair of UFixed18 maintenance and fundingFee values used to initialize the product, C.maintenance() returns the stored maintenance value (the one provided at initialize); the mutant returns fundingFee() instead, so when the fuzzed maintenance != fundingFee the mutant will produce a different return value causing the property to fail.

For any pair of UFixed18 values provided to initialize the product (maintenance and fundingFee), the correct contract's maintenance() returns the stored maintenance value; the mutant returns fundingFee() instead, so when the fuzzed maintenance != fundingFee the mutant will return a different value and the property is violated.

For any stored maintenance value m, calling maintenance() returns exactly the stored maintenance (i.e., not doubled); the mutant that returns m+m will produce a different return for some m (e.g., any non-zero m).

For any stored maintenance value m, the contract's maintenance() returns exactly the stored maintenance m; the mutant doubles it (returns 2*m) so there exist inputs (any m != 0) where the returned value differs.
